notes.title: New Locomotion, Blocking, and Fake Snaps - July Title Update
notes.content:
What’s up, Maximum Football fans! 

We are excited to publish our first major update to Maximum Football since launching into 1.0 last month. This update includes a number of bug fixes, gameplay improvements, and feature updates designed to address some of the main points of feedback we’ve been hearing from the community since  1.0 launch. 

In our most recent Dev Blog, we shared that a new CPU playcalling system was in the works. During testing over the past week, we identified several areas that need further refinement. To ensure it meets our standards and delivers the best experience, we’ve decided to move the release of this feature to the August update.

Here’s what’s included in the update. 
New Locomotion[previewyoutube="irTmni1o1D8;full"][/previewyoutube]
We’ve continued our work on refining player movement to make gameplay feel smoother, more responsive, and more lifelike. This update includes several key changes to how players move on the field:

Speed-Based Animations: Players now transition more naturally between movement speeds. As a player accelerates, their running animations update to match—limbs move faster, and strides lengthen to reflect the pace.

Improved Transitions: We’ve smoothed out the transitions between idle and movement, especially when changing directions. This is most noticeable on screen plays and short routes—where previously, receivers would hesitate after catching the ball. Now, they’ll fluidly transition into their next movement, getting upfield more quickly and realistically.

These updates are part of our ongoing effort to make every movement—from a quick cut to a breakaway run—feel as clean and satisfying as possible.
Updated Pass Blocking
Blocking has been a key area of focus leading into 1.0, and while earlier updates improved run blocking and special teams performance, this update zeroes in on pass protection.

Pocket Formation Improvements: Offensive linemen are now better at forming and maintaining the pocket. Rather than chasing defenders out of position, they focus on threats directly in front of them—helping to seal off interior gaps and reinforce the wall around the quarterback.

QB-Aware Blocking Logic: Linemen now have improved awareness of the quarterback’s movement. They’ll work to steer pass rushers away from the QB’s current position, helping reduce pressure from blindside or broken-pocket scenarios.

These changes are designed to create a more realistic and reliable pass protection experience—and give your quarterback the time they need to make the right throw.
Fake Snap
You can now use a fake snap to keep the defense guessing.

Tap RB (Xbox) / R1 (PlayStation) at the line of scrimmage to perform a hard count.

Use it to try and draw the defense offsides or disrupt their timing before the snap.

Mix this into your pre-snap routine to gain an edge against aggressive defenders.

Full Patch NotesHere’s what else is included in this month’s update:

Gameplay changes
Reworked basic locomotion for smoother, more natural transitions

Added the ability to use fake snaps

Reworked pass blocking behavior and improvements for run blocking

Temporarily disabled AI dive tackles, we are very curious what you as the community think about this change, we are looking for feedback on the feel of the game now

Added an indicator for the ball in case a fumble happens

Added better onboarding for new players via drills

Onside kick power is now reduced

Non-targeted receivers now switch to jog when they realize the pass is not thrown to them

New catch and kick catch animations added

Added more tackle and broken tackle animations

Added new celebration animations for AI

Improvements made for head tracking (DL, LB, DB, Catching, Post play)

Dynasty | Adjusted recruit contact while on low prestige. Adjusted top stats number

Dynasty | Adjusted stadiums for bowls and playoffs.

Added KR and PR yards gained to the Total Yards calculation
Bugfixes
Various audio improvements for sound timing and commentary fixes

Fixed an issue where the AI could still go into hurry-up offense while calling a timeout

Fixed an issue with Cover 2 Gap Control Pinch leading to instant sacks or tackle for loss

Fixed an issue with receivers not being able to transition to movement once a catch has been made (this is most visible with screen plays)

Fixed various issues which could cause hurry-up offense to have issues due to players failing to line up properly on offense

Fixed run plays not always showing routes on field

QB being tackled after throwing a “pass” will not trigger rushing stats.

MPL - Fix jersey conflicts on adding players to roster.

MPL - Fix penalization when leaving team selection

MPL - Reset winstreak on vsCPU games

Fixed - Onfield elements will display the same play clock value as the HUD.

Fixed "Extra drills" (such as speed burst drill) not being progressable in dynasty.

Fixed Mouthguards not being visible in multiplayer

Fixed an issue in-game where sometimes players on the same side (e.g. offense or defense) were seen with the same jersey numbers

Fixed an issue where changing sides in the team selector before a match could reset settings like uniforms and playbooks

Fixed rushing yard statistics not working with pitchout plays

Various smaller bugfixes
Customization
Jersey pattern texture fixes

Fixed bench coloring issue in Cobblestone Park

Fixed the field stripes being invisible in Castonguay Field

Added back the “Apply for all” function in customization

MPL - Fix for going into the lobby with the wrong team uniform.
Other improvements
Crash fixes

Significantly reduced build size on PC

Various optimization improvements

Profanity Filter | Added more names to whitelist, including community-requested last names

Improved snow on lower spec machines

Fixed some weirdness with shadows in snow

Various improvements to animations for the locomotion rework

notes.title: Maximum Football 1.0 Arrives June
notes.content:
Mark your calendars: Maximum Football officially launches into 1.0 on June 17 

After launching into Steam Early Access and Xbox Game Preview last year, we’ve delivered over a dozen updates and hotfixes to improve gameplay, enhance quality of life, and expand the game's core features. From Coach Mode and couch multiplayer to invite-based online play and full Dynasty spectating, many of the most impactful additions came directly from your feedback. 

[previewyoutube=qgcqn2AZp0M;full][/previewyoutube]

Now, we’re gearing up for the next chapter. On June 17, we leave Early Access behind and take our biggest step yet—with new features, new players, and a brand-new season of content. But before we kick things off, let’s take a look at what 1.0 means for the future of Maximum Football. 

What Does 1.0 Mean 

Reaching 1.0 is a major milestone—but it’s far from the finish line. Launching out of Early Access means we can bring Maximum Football to new players and platforms, while continuing to refine the core gameplay and deliver the features our community has asked for. 

Development isn’t slowing down. We’ll keep pushing regular updates, introducing new features, and expanding the game with fresh content. Our goal is to make Maximum Football the ultimate sandbox for building your dream football experience. 

Now, let’s dive into what’s coming with the 1.0 launch. 

New Features 

Maximum Football on PlayStation 5! 

You’ve been asking—and we’re thrilled to deliver. With the 1.0 launch, Maximum Football is officially coming to PlayStation 5. Starting June 17, PlayStation players can finally join in and start building their ultimate football universe. 

Weather
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43609941/d23c458dd07359bf5b3f70c10d3a88fb71fda257.jpg
Until now, every game has taken place under clear skies. That changes with 1.0. Rain and snow are being added to Maximum Football, bringing new atmosphere and challenge to your gameday experience.  

Stadium Customization 

Make your stadium a true reflection of your team’s identity. With the 1.0 launch, you’ll be able to personalize your field color and stadium seating to match your team’s branding. It’s your home—make it look the part. 

Multiple Team Logos 
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43609941/5b437b61e4682a0e7850693547df6657db3362d5.jpg
College football teams don’t stop at just one logo—and now, neither do you. With 1.0, you can upload up to nine logos per team and use them across your uniforms. Build a brand that feels as dynamic as the team you’ve created. 

Season 3 

June 17 doesn’t just mark the launch of 1.0—it also kicks off a brand-new season of content (we’ll reveal the full theme soon!). We’re using your feedback to improve how Season Pass content is earned and what’s included. 

First, in addition to weekly and seasonal challenges, we’re introducing passive XP—you’ll now make progress on your Season Pass just by finishing games. Play your way and keep moving forward. 

We’re also expanding the rewards on both the free and premium tracks. That includes more variety, higher-value items, and not one, but two stadiums: 


 The premium reward at Tier 1 gives pass holders a brand-new stadium right from the start. 
 The free reward at Tier 50 offers a second stadium for all players who complete the pass. 

Updated Animations and Anatomy 
We’re packing in a wide range of new animations for 1.0, including an updated kickoff sequence and improvements to catching, running, and tackling. You’ll also notice non-gameplay animations—players reacting on the sidelines, motioning between plays, and more—that bring added life and immersion to every snap. 

Beyond animations, we’ve refined how player bodies respond to the action. Players now move more naturally, track plays with greater awareness, and interact with each other more believably during collisions and transitions. 

But enough talk—you want to see this in action! Come back next Tuesday for a full half of 1.0 gameplay IN THE SNOW!

FAQs

1. What game modes will be available on June 17th?

On June 17th, you will be able to play Exhibition Mode, Dynasty, Maximum Pro League, Couch Multiplayer, Coach Mode, and Invite Multiplayer, as well as create teams in the Maximum Football Customization Suite.

2. What platforms will Maximum Football be available on when it releases on June 17th?

Maximum Football will be available to play on Steam, PlayStation 5, and Xbox Series X|S.

3. What editions of the game will be available?

Base Game (Free):

 Maximum Pro League
 Single Player Exhibition Mode
 Customization Suite
 Dynasty Starter Mode (Free Access to initial seasons)

Dynasty Edition ($19.99):

 Base Game
 Unlimited Access to Dynasty Mode
 Dynasty Pack (Dynasty gloves, helmet, pants, mask, and fireball celebration)

Legend Edition ($39.99):

 Base Game
 Unlimited Dynasty Access and Dynasty Pack
 Unlimited Franchise Access and Franchise Pack (Coming in 2025)
 Legend Pack (Legend stadium, mouthguard, 1200 max stacks, and knee drop celebration)


4. Is Franchise releasing with 1.0?

Franchise won’t be available on June 17th. We are taking a bit more time to get it right. Be on the lookout for more information about Franchise later this summer.

5. Will crossplay be available on June 17th?

No. In order to ensure the most stable online performance on launch day, crossplay will not be available. Crossplay will be added to the game in a future update.

6. Is the game still planned for release on PS4 and Xbox One?

Yes!

7. Does the team still plan to release regular updates now that the game is in 1.0?

Absolutely! 1.0 is the beginning of the next chapter of Maximum Football, and the feedback we receive from our existing community, returning players, and newcomers to Maximum Football will continue to shape the future of this game.

notes.title: Dev Blog: Weather, Stadium Customization, and Blocking
notes.content:
What’s going on, Maximum Football crew!  

Luke here from the Maximum Football team, kicking off a new regular check-in series where we break down what we’re working on—and what you can look forward to in Maximum Football. 

These check-ins are a way for us to pull back the curtain and bring you deeper into our development process. Maximum Football is a game being shaped by its community, and we want to keep that collaboration going strong. 

What We’re Working On 
Last week, we launched our first major patch of Season 2. We’ve received ample feedback from you – thank you for sharing your suggestions.  

MPL Depth Chart Issues 
We saw some reports of users who encountered a bug where they got duplicate versions of their MPL cards. 

We identified the source of this issue and pushed a hotfix for this bug this week.   

Blocking Improvements 
We made a lot of adjustments to blocking in our most recent patch, and we’ve seen from the community that this has been a big improvement over the way the game played pre-patch. However, we are still seeing lingering issues especially on special teams  that we want to address in our next update. Blocked punts and blocked FGs are still happening at too high a rate for our liking, and we want to continue to make changes to improve the effectiveness of special teams.  

Chasing down some lingering clock issues 
Our hotfix last week addressed a number of clock issues that players were encountering following the patch. However, we are still monitoring a few player reports of lingering clock issues. If you see any weird behavior from the clock, please drop it in the comments or in our #Feedback channel on Discord.  

Looking Ahead 
We recently announced that Maximum Football is coming to PlayStation 5 this summer—and our team is hard at work preparing for that launch. That means polishing core gameplay and introducing features that will debut with the 1.0 release. 

Weather Effects 

Rain and snow are on the horizon! As mentioned in a previous mailbag, cosmetic weather will be added for 1.0. This will be a visual-only update to start, with gameplay-affecting weather planned for later this year.

New Playcalling System 
Football is about the Jimmies and the Joes, but it is also about the X’s and the O’s. And we are hard at work on a new playcalling system that is going to add a new layer of realism to CPU coaching. This system is going to help address several areas that we’ve heard community feedback on including: 

 Late game playcalling and awareness 
 Run and pass balance 
 Defensive playcalling

We have this system currently working on our development build, but before we release it out to the public, we have a very simple philosophy -- “is this better than the system that we currently have.” Until we can answer that with a resounding yes, we are going to continue to polish it.  

Stadium Customization
Customization is a pillar of Maximum Football. We want to give players the tools they need to make the teams they want to make. The next addition we are making to that end is the ability to customize the color of the turf and the seats in your stadium. From various natural grass colors to vibrant artificial turf, you will soon be able to express your style in brand new ways in Maximum Football.

Mailbag: Your Questions, Answered 
In the past, we have done monthly mailbags, giving you all the opportunity to submit your questions for the development team to answer. Now, we want to answer your questions more regularly, so we will be adding a Q&A as a part of these Dev Blogs!  

So, drop your questions in the comments below or in the #Monthly-Mailbag channel in our Discord, and we may choose to answer them in our next Dev Blog.  

In Case You Missed It 
Last week’s patch focused on stabilizing key areas of gameplay and introduced a long-requested feature from the community. Here’s what’s in the latest patch: 

 Couch Multiplayer – Face off with friends on the same console and battle it out for bragging rights. 
 Offensive Line Fixes – We’ve tackled several issues that made blocking feel underpowered. Both pass protection and run blocking should now feel more balanced and consistent. 
 Offsides Penalties – The invisible wall at the line of scrimmage is gone. Jump the snap early? That’s an offsides. 
 Hurry-Up Offense – Run a fast-paced offense with the new hurry-up functionality—perfect for two-minute drills or keeping defenses on their heels. 
 Gameplay Sliders – We're introducing an experimental feature that lets you tweak gameplay to your liking. Sliders will be available in Exhibition and Exhibition Coach Mode only for now. 

You can check out the full patch notes here. We also released two subsequent hotfixes to address things like a spectate bug, an issue with pump fakes, and reincluding day/night selection.

notes.title: Gang Tackling, Left Handed Quarterbacks, and Customization - May Monthly Mailbag
notes.content:
Hey Maximum Football crew — what’s up? 

We’re trying something new with the Monthly Mailbag. In the past, we’ve done these as videos, but the reality is: there’s a whole team of folks working behind the scenes on Maximum Football, and a blog gives us a better way to tap into their insights. 

By shifting to this format, I can pull in answers from across the dev team and give you a fuller look at what’s happening under the hood. So with that—let’s dive into your questions. 

What has Unreal Engine 5 enable this team to do with Maximum Football that other engines wouldn’t have allowed? 

We chose Unreal Engine 5 for two big reasons. First, it lets us hit next‑level graphics faster and more efficiently — real‑time global illumination, super‑realistic materials, and all the visual polish you expect from a modern title. 

Second, UE5’s robust physics system powers the core of our gameplay. From the ball’s arc through the air to the trench battles at the line of scrimmage, every collision and movement is driven by real‑time physics calculations. That level of fidelity simply wouldn’t be possible in most other engines. 

When is the next animation package being added? 

Animations are constantly being added to Maximum Football. Seriously. Every single update we release includes new animations and updated animations. Starting in February, our updates have addressed locomotion with a new sprint animation  

We have another mocap session that’s planned for this summer where we will continue to capture new blocks, catches, tackles, running animations, and more!  

With hurry up offense now in the game, where is the team at with addressing CPU late-half clock management? 

This is still a work-in-progress for us, but we are making strides to not only improve the CPU’s late game situational awareness, but overhaul the CPU playcalling system altogether.  

For now, you will see the CPU leveraging the new hurry up mechanic in late-game situations when it makes sense.  

As for the remainder of the overhaul, our philosophy is simple, we will continue to polish it on our end while asking ourself “is this new system better than the system we have in the game now.” The moment we can answer that with a resounding yes, we will implement the new system into the game!  

Is the team working on adding gang tackling? 

Absolutely—gang tackling is on our roadmap! We’re currently fine‑tuning our 1v1 tackle mechanics to get them just right, and once that’s locked in, we’ll shift our focus to adding realistic gang‑tackle dynamics. It won’t be in our 1.0 launch, but it’s definitely coming in a future update. Stay tuned! 

Right now, there are only right-handed quarterbacks in the game, are there plans to add left-handers? 

We do plan to add left‑handed QBs. Beyond simply flipping our right‑handed throws, southpaws bring unique release angles and body mechanics that we want to nail down authentically. We’re currently evaluating whether we can mirror existing animations or if we need a dedicated mocap session for left‑handed throws. Either way, you’ll see true lefty signal‑callers in a future update. 

What updates to customization are coming?  

Customization is a core pillar of what we are building with Maximum Football, and we want to continue to add ways for players to express their creativity on the field. So, here’s some of the stuff we have coming up soon.  

Custom field colors: For Season 2, we introduced Seaside Park, which featured our first new colored turf. But soon, any field in Maximum Football will be able to sport a different colored turf, as well as different colored seats throughout your stadium.  

Custom endzones and additional field logo customization are on the long term roadmap to give you even more options for customization.

notes.title: Couch Multiplayer, Updated Blocking and More Now Available
notes.content:
Hey everyone, 

Thank you for continuing to support Maximum Football! Since the launch of Season 2: Vice Blitz, we’ve been blown away by your passion, gameplay clips, and honest feedback. Your input helps us shape the future of the game, and this latest patch is a direct result of your voices being heard. 

Today, we are releasing the first patch of the season. Let’s dive into some of the biggest improvements coming your way: 

️🛋️ Couch Multiplayer Is Here
Grab a friend and settle the score locally—you can now play head-to-head on the same system. Whether you're going head-to-head in a rivalry game or testing out team builds, Couch Multiplayer is finally live. 

🧱 Offensive Line Fixes (Thanks to You!) 
We heard your frustration loud and clear: the O-line was getting bullied. Defensive linemen were breaking through far too easily, wrecking the run game and collapsing the pocket in seconds. 

This patch delivers improved offensive line play—giving you more time to survey the field and execute your gameplan. It’s a better balance between offense and defense, and a huge quality-of-life change that came directly from community feedback 

🚫 Offsides Penalties Are Now Live 
The era of running at the line pre-snap without consequences is over. Jumping the snap will now result in an offsides penalty, especially cracking down on online players who were abusing the invisible wall to gain an unfair edge. 

Clean up your timing—or be prepared to march backward. 

🏃‍♂️ Hurry-Up Offense 
Add some tempo to your attack! You can now run a no-huddle offense by holding Y after the play. Your squad will hustle to the line, giving you the chance to catch the defense off guard and keep drives alive. 

Those are the biggest highlights—but we’ve packed this patch with a lot more. Keep reading for the full list of detailed patch notes below. 

Known Issues
We are aware of an issue in this patch that is causing users to pump fake and lose the ability to pass. The team is working on a hot fix that will address this issue ASAP, and we will post an announcement when it is available. 

There are a few other known issues present in this build that we will fix in a future update. 

 some issues with the controller assignment for the 2nd user for couch play
 users may encounter an error when trying to access MPL; this gets fixed with a game restart
 there are some issues with registering the loss when disconnecting from an online ranked match


Full Patch Notes

Gameplay:

 Onside kicks now work reliably even if you call a timeout after setting kick power, and crash‑related uniform syncing when joining sessions has been fixed. 
 Drill exercises (pass defense, hot routes, etc.) no longer get stuck after touchdown catches or when selecting plays. 
 Recovered‑punt touchdowns now correctly award possession 
 Star‑player indicator logic has been added. 
 Penalties are now observed by the rules engine, and AI will decline unnecessary penalties when they cost more yards. 
 “No‑Huddle” offenses and hurry‑up sequences no longer leave players in awkward formations or teleport defensive players. 
 Client‑side join logic was fixed so switching into coach mode—and other lobby privileges—don’t reset unexpectedly. 
 Exhibition‑mode stats challenges now track correctly (including two‑point conversions, missed kicks, and challenge progress), and match history statistics have been cleaned up. 
 Conversion kicks that miss no longer trigger a touchback, and delay‑of‑game positioning on extra‑point tries is now accurate. 
 Sideline players and coaches react dynamically—with animations and head‑tracking—to real‑time events like big plays and injuries. 
 Overtime coach suggestions now respect whether you’re allowed a conversion kick, and the new overtime ruleset is available in menu settings. 
 The play clock pauses during instant replays and auto‑rewind, with correct timing after turnovers and penalties (40 seconds NCAA, 25 seconds Pro). 
 Substitutions, depth‑chart views, and challenge‑system upgrades have been revamped: 
 Substitution panels now initialize properly. 
 Challenge values never go negative, and quest requirements update dynamically. 
 “Fair catch,” “pickup,” and “block” actions on punts are now handled correctly by both AI and user, and special hot‑route pass‑block options were added. 
 The profanity filter has been expanded and whitelist fixes applied. 
 Post‑play cameras now offer multiple perspectives, and you can disable auto‑replay if you prefer. 
 Controller LED flashes, input handling during cinematics, and UI prompts (e.g., waiting‑for‑match, error pop‑ups) have been polished to avoid duplicates or misfires. 
 Practice‑mode improvements include stable previous‑play selection, non‑conflicting keybinds, and accurate replay behavior when skipping cut‑scenes. 
 Demo/test features were added for QA (e.g., forced practice‑map states, debug property flags) to facilitate easier testing of new match conditions. 

Animations

 Tweaked the new “strider” movement animations and added smooth blendspaces for it. 
 Introduced a set of new coach animations. 
 Added various sideline behaviors  
 Updated block‑engagement montages in the animation database for smoother look. 
 Added notifies and sync markers to all new strider animations for better timing. 
 Motion‑matching is now applied to all passing animations for more natural movement. 
 Refined the sprint animation based on design feedback. 
 Added new jump and 360‑turn catch animations to diversify receptions. 
 Adjusted open‑field blocking animations to look more dynamic. 
 Implemented diagonal QB movement animations so quarterbacks can move and pass on the run. 
 Polished several of the new catch animations and ensured they use the correct montage slots. 
 Fine‑tuned scramble (QB run) animations for better realism. 
 Introduced multiple new catch variations (CatchRun series and pump‑fake animations). 
 Slowed down post‑touchdown celebration animations for dramatic effect. 
 Improved sideline “messing with shoulder pads” and “helmet” idle behaviors on the bench. 
 Refined stationary QB and passing animations to blend more smoothly into movement. 
 Fixed bone‑orientation issues in kick‑catch animations so feet and hands align correctly. 
 Added quick‑pass variants and modified several existing quick‑pass animations. 
 Updated referee animations, including signals and idle behaviors. 
 Added “disappointment” animations for dropped catches. 
 Enhanced banking and locomotion animations to support the new speed‑management system. 
 Implemented foot‑lock prevention tags so characters don’t get stuck in place during catch transitions. 
 Fixed an issue where sideline players could spawn twice on client machines. 
 Disabled lower‑body locomotion when entering catch montages to avoid sliding feet. 
 Added a number of new stadium cinematics.  

Dynasty

 Fixed several underlying issues so dynasty mode runs without errors. 
 Added dynasty‑specific upgrades for the challenge system. 
 Ensured all dynasty activities now trigger and record as intended. 
 Made a small UI tweak to improve consistency in the dynasty menus. 
 Corrected the team-selection logic so the right franchise is always loaded. 
 Fixed various dynasty UI glitches across multiple screens, including roster, achievements, and settings panels. 
 Enabled you to view your team’s depth chart while spectating a dynasty game. 
 Updated overtime coach suggestions in dynasty to honor whether a conversion kick is allowed. 
 Began tracking your franchise’s active team during live gameplay events for better stats and logs. 
 Improved navigation so menu focus never gets stuck while moving through dynasty screens. 
 Applied general performance and stability fixes tied to dynasty progression and milestone events. 
 Updated injuries in dynasty mode. 
 Blocked user inputs during dynasty loading screens to prevent accidental selections and refined achievement tracking for “Match” and “Changed Up.” 
 Corrected two achievements (“Dealin’” and “Top of the Class”) so they unlock under the proper conditions.

MPL

 Reset local player data correctly if a client disconnects from the network. 
 Fixed various matchmaking errors that could recreate sessions incorrectly when offline.

notes.title: Welcome to Season 2: Vice Blitz
notes.content:
Last season, you took to the field aboard the iconic Aircraft Carrier Stadium. This time, we’re bringing the action to the sunny shores of the coastal Southeast. Get ready to suit up on the lime green turf of Seaside Park, a brand-new stadium surrounded by palm trees and coastal vibes. 

[previewyoutube=j9oyxpWOTkE;full][/previewyoutube]

But Season 2 isn’t just about a fresh backdrop and new cosmetics—we’ve also made meaningful changes based on your feedback. Progression is now faster, more flexible, and even more rewarding, making it easier to earn the content you want while playing the way you enjoy. 

As always, the Season Pass includes both free and premium rewards at every tier, featuring card packs, cosmetics, celebrations, and in-game currency. And don’t worry—if you decide to upgrade to the premium pass later in the season, you’ll instantly unlock any premium rewards you would have earned thanks to your progression. 

Changes To Progress in Season 2 

We’ve made some adjustments to the way progression works in Season 2 based on feedback from the community. This season, you’ll earn rewards more quickly and have greater flexibility when it comes to completing challenges across different game modes. 

Let’s start with progression. In Season 1, we heard that some challenges felt a bit too specific or demanding, which made it harder for some players to stay on track. For Season 2, we’ve fine-tuned the difficulty of weekly and seasonal challenges to make them more approachable—so you can keep moving forward and unlocking rewards at a steady pace. 

We’re also expanding how and where you can complete challenges. Now, your stats will count toward weekly and seasonal progress whether you’re playing online or offline MPL, Dynasty mode, or Exhibition Mode. However you choose to play, your progress will follow. 

Defensive Hot Routes 

We’re adding more control to the defensive side of the ball in Season 2 with the introduction of defensive hot routes. You can now adjust individual defender assignments pre-snap, giving you the tools to counter what you’re seeing from the offense in real time. Whether you want to put a linebacker into a hook zone, assign a cornerback to man coverage, or send an extra rusher off the edge, defensive hot routes let you make smart, strategic adjustments on the fly—just like a real defensive coordinator. 

Alternate Jersey Selection in Dynasty Mode 

Season 2 brings more customization to your Dynasty experience with the addition of alternate jerseys. You’ll now have the ability to create alternate uniforms at any point during your Dynasty and choose which look your team will take the field in before each game. Whether you're designing a bold new look for rivalry week or just switching things up for fun, alternate jerseys give you more ways to show off your team’s identity and make every matchup feel unique. 

Coach Mode in Online Exhibition 

We’re also expanding the flexibility of how you play with an update to Coach Mode. Previously limited to offline play, Coach Mode is now available in online exhibition games—allowing you to take on your friends head-to-head while calling the shots from the sideline. Whether you're testing your play-calling skills or just prefer a more strategic, hands-off experience, you can now compete online in Coach Mode and prove who’s the better football mind.

What’s up, Maximum Football gang. We have a brand new update for you, and this one includes a feature that’s been requested since before we launched back in November – Coach Mode! But that’s not all. Here’s a look at some of the biggest changes you’ll notice in this update. 

Coach Mode

Don the headset or the old Lombardi fedora and outstrategize your opponent with coach mode. {STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43609941/d90be57ac5738e2a426a12b4056d5121016fa258.jpg
              
To activate Coach Mode, simply enter an exhibition or dynasty game and from the team select screen, press the menu key or V. You will see coach mode activated over your team name. Now, start your game and call your plays. You will have the ability to toggle the spectator cameras during the game as you coach. 

Sandbox Progression

We know that an XP based progression system in Dynasty isn’t everyone’s cup of tea, so we are introducing Sandbox Progression in this week’s patch. This allows players to bypass the current XP system and freely change the individual ratings for players on their rosters and the rosters of other teams however they want! You can toggle this option from the settings menu in Dynasty mode. 

Improve Running Animations and Locomotions

We are currently in the middle of a massive locomotion overhaul in Maximum Football, and this update is the first step of a few over the never few patches to reword player movement in the game. You will notice some new running animations including a more aggressive sprint where a ball carrier puts his head down running with the ball. Player movement is also improved in both fluidity and responsiveness. 

Sportsmanship in MPL

We want to ensure the online experience is enjoyable for players who commit their time to competing against others in MPL. To that end, we have made some changes to the way sportsmanship impacts matchmaking. Now, the game is going to attempt to matchmake players with similar sportsmanship scores against one another online.

 Native 4K support for an enhanced visual experience

notes.title: Maximum Football MPL Update – Card Pack Fix Coming Next Week!
notes.content:

After thorough investigation, we realized that to ensure Maximum Football and MPL function as intended, we needed to migrate our entire backend system to a new provider. notes.title: Card Pack Issue Update for Maximum Pro League Players
notes.content:
We want to provide an update regarding the current issue affecting card packs in Maximum Pro League (MPL). We are aware that new users attempting to enter MPL, as well as existing users trying to open card packs, are encountering an error.

We have identified the root cause and are actively working on a solution to restore normal functionality to card pack openings in MPL.

Current Situation

 Existing Card Packs: If you attempt to open a card pack already in your inventory, you will receive a timeout error or a message indicating the card was not created. The pack will remain in your inventory and will not disappear. Once the issue is resolved, you will be able to open all packs you have purchased.
 New Purchases: If you attempt to purchase a card pack you don’t currently own, the same error will occur. However, after restarting the game, the currency will be deducted, and the pack will appear in your inventory (marked with “Free x1” in the store). These packs will remain unopened until the issue is fixed.
 New Users: MPL relies on the creation of new cards to build your initial team. As a result, new users will not be able to access MPL until the issue is resolved. All starter packs will be available to open once the fix is in place

Timeline and Next Steps:
A fix is in development and will be available in our next update. This fix will take some time and will require a patch for both Steam and Xbox. Until then, we encourage users to NOT attempt to purchase or open packs in MPL. 

We understand the frustration this may cause and apologize for the inconvenience. Challenges such as this come with the territory of an early access launch, and we are committed to getting MPL back up and running as soon as possible. We appreciate your patience and will continue to provide updates as we implement solutions, including a permanent fix planned for the near future.

Thank you for your understanding and continued support.

notes.title: Our 2025 Maximum Football Roadmap
notes.content:
As the year comes to a close, it’s only natural for us to look back and take stock of where we’ve been. It’s been a banner year for the Maximum Football team with the game launching to Steam Early Access and Xbox Game Preview at the end of the year. It’s been a long road to get to where we are and there have been a lot of blood, sweat, and tears poured into this project. We are so grateful for everyone in our community for the faith they’ve had in us and their willingness to come along for the ride. 

In 2024, we launched our first playable Beta during the Steam Summer Next Fest where we were able to see the first pieces of feedback from the community. Since then, we have made thousands of changes to the game in the lead up to our Early Access launch in November. 

With the game now out in the wild, we have gathered hundreds of pieces of feedback and released four updates that have addressed some of the most pressing feedback we’ve received from you. 

But the end of the year is also a time for us to look forward. While we are proud of where Maximum Football is as we round out the year, we are even more excited about what’s to come in 2025, and we want you to get excited along with us. 

To that end, we are FINALLY ready to reveal our 2025 Roadmap listing features and improvements we will be focusing on when our calendar turns over to January. 

Here’s a handy graphic to help you better understand what to expect in the first half of the new year. 

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43609941/11aaa1717c84626e7e9d6594f76621e01afe5be4.jpg

Now, let’s break it down. 

Major Features

Since releasing the game, and even prior to, we’ve been listening to the community about what’s most important to them to have included in the game. So our focus for the new year will be as follows:
[olist]
 Coach Mode: A highly requested feature from our hardcore sim audience, Coach Mode will allow you to serve as your teams playcaller while allowing the CPU to run the plays once the call is in. 
 Invite Multiplayer: What are sports games without a little friendly (or heated) competition. In 2025, we will be adding friend invites to our online offerings.
 Couch co-op: Even better than a digital rivalry is an in-person one. Next year, we will release an update that allows players to compete against one another on the same system. 
 Crossplay: One of the keys to a healthy online ecosystem is having a big player base that allows for quick queues and solid connections. That’s why we will be opening up crossplay some time in the new year to allow Steam and Xbox players (and eventually PlayStation) to compete against one another in MPL. 
 Franchise Mode: The professional equivalent to Dynasty mode, Franchise mode will allow you to take over as the General Manager of a pro sports franchise in a customizable experience. We will reveal more about Franchise mode as we approach its release. 
[/olist]

[previewyoutube=edqGugDMUYI;full][/previewyoutube]

Other Features

The 5 items listed above are considered major mode and functionality additions, but they don’t represent the only updates we will be working on. We are also committed to adding other, smaller user-requested features to the game. These include:
[olist]
 Weather
 Screens, Draws, and other offensive plays
 Defensive hot routes
 More playcalling options
 Team and roster sharing
 UI adjustments for Roster Management
[/olist]
This is by no means an exhaustive list, but it shows a few key items the team is actively working to add to the game. 

Ongoing Updates

Finally, there are several aspects of improvements that will be continuous efforts from the team. We will continue to monitor community feedback for ways to improve quality of life for our players, making adjustments to the things we see coming up the most. Online matchmaking and stability will continue to improve with each update, as well. 

Lastly, we are in the process of overhauling our animation system and adding tons of new animations to account for different situations on the field. This will result in a more realistic on-field product both visually and physically. 

All of the information including timelines and features are subject to change. We are still committed to listening to our audience and making the adjustments that are most important to you moving forward. Stay tuned for real-time updates as features start to roll out. 

Thank You From the Maximum Football Team

With the year now coming to a close, we want to thank you for playing and giving us your thoughts on the game. We are going to be winding down for the end of the year to take a break and recharge with our families for the holidays. We will be back with our next update in January. Until then, continue to build your ultimate football universe in Maximum Football. 

See you in the new year!

notes.title: Our Next Update, What We Are Working On, and How You Can Help
notes.content:
What’s going on everybody. Luke here from the Maximum Football Team here to talk about a few things including our next update, what the team’s working on now, and how you in the Maximum Football community can continue to help us improve the game. 

You can check out the video here. If you'd rather read, the script for the video is attached below. 

[previewyoutube=iiy4Oj8f0DE;full][/previewyoutube]

New Update Coming December 10th

First, let’s talk about the next title update for Maximum Football. With the game releasing on Xbox Game Preview on December 10th, we are holding our next Steam update to coincide with that release and it’s going to include a TON of updates and fixes. 

For starters, we are adding a number of new plays to offensive playbooks including playaction. Now, you can set your run game and then beat your opponent over the top with the playfake. This change includes dozens of AI fixes and adjustments to account for the new playtype. 

We are also adding in some situational plays like QB kneel, spike, and onside kick. These options will allow you to manage your late game strategy more effectively. 

The passing game continues to receive some tweaks and adjustments to make it more responsive. Including making the receivers attack the ball in the air more naturally, reducing defensive back’s catching abilities in traffic so that you will see less catches after being tipped, fixing a bug where receivers would stop their route early, 

We have seen clips of diving defenders passing through ball carriers. The next update will give a temporary fix to this issue, allowing the cpu to resolve the play as intended. However, you might see some wonkiness in the animation as we have to do some motion capture to fully resolve the problem.

The update also fixes a ton of bugs including the soft lock on kickoff’s in MPL, challenge progress not tracking appropriately, a few nano blitzes that were being exploited, some issues with possession logic on two point conversions, and more. 

You can also now flip your plays from the playcall menu and during an audible. 

Players are now no longer able to grief online opponents with endless delay of game penalties. Now, if you abuse delay of game penalty three times in a row, it will result in a change of possession and a reduction in your sportsmanship grade. With each subsequent delay of game penalty the number of allowed delay of games will be reduced by one. 

We have also made some tweaks to our profanity filter since it was being a bit overly aggressive… 

There are a ton of other changes included in this update that you will be able to check out when we publish the full change log next week. 

What We Are Working On

When it comes to online play, we are actively tracking exploits and overpowered strategies in an attempt to balance gameplay and make online matches play closer to a real life game. This includes fixes to low trajectory kick-offs, overpowered lead blocking plays, adjustments to how AI defenders assess threats to QBs escaping the pocket, and more. 

Dynasty mode continues to be an area of focus for the team and we are tracking and investigating a number of reported issues. Changes like adjusting quarter length mid-season, adding the ability to select jerseys pre-game,  adjustments to how AI upgrades their players, and more. 

We also know two of our most highly requested features are online, invite-only exhibitions for you to play with friends, and coach mode. I can tell you that these are high priority items for the team and while we don’t currently have an exact timeline for their release, they are actively being worked on. 

The team is continuing to work on new modes and features that will be rolled out throughout early access. And we will talk about those more when publish our Maximum Football Early Access Roadmap later this month. 

How You Can Help

The internal changelog for our last 3 updates has hundreds of items on it, and nearly every change can be tied directly back to an Instagram comment, Steam Forum post, Discord bug report, or other community feedback area. When we say we want to build this game alongside you, we meant it. We are listening and we are working tirelessly to make this the best simulation football game on the market. 

Here’s how you can help us continue to work towards that goal. 

Follow us! Wherever you are watching this content, follow and subscribe and comment changes that you want to see. No matter how big or small. From bug fixes to mode additions, we want to know what you think will make this game great. 

Join our Discord. Me, Micah, and other members of the Maximum Football team are always hanging out in there and engaging with the community. So if you have feedback, feature requests, questions, or just want to share a sick play or custom team you’ve made, our Discord is the place to be. 

December 10th is a big day for us. This update is dropping, Maximum Football comes to Xbox Game Preview, and our first season pass Grid Iron Glory drops. We will see you then.

When you download Maximum Football, you will be able to jump right into making teams, editing players, and competing on the gridiron. Here’s what you can expect to have access to the moment you download Maximum Football on Steam.

notes.title: Introducing Maximum Pro League
notes.content:
In Maximum Football, we wanted to create a fun and competitive card game that also maintained our core vision of allowing players to create their ultimate football universe. Enter Maximum Pro League. 

Maximum Pro League (MPL) is Maximum Football’s unique take on the deckbuilding sports game that allows you to take the game’s powerful customization tools and build the online squad that YOU want to compete with. This is a mode unlike any other in the sports genre. Here’s how. 
[previewyoutube=1_y3bsBj7dI;full][/previewyoutube]

Starting Your Team

In MPL, you won’t be restricted to selecting from a collection of pre-existing teams while you unlock more options. No. In the MPL menu, you will find the exact same team creator that is available to you in the single-player game. Upload custom logos, create home, away, and alternate uniforms, and set your team’s name, city and playbooks. You MPL team is your opportunity to express your creativity on the field. 

When you first log into MPL, you will be given over 60 cards to start your team. These cards can range across MPL’s four rarity levels: common, rare, epic, and legend. This will serve as your starter team and the foundation from which you will build your team. While the players on each card are auto-generated by the game, you can customize the details of any player in your deck. Rename them, change their appearance, and customize their equipment. 
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43609941/935f6ee65120adaddc61fa9c13fa30fe83a50fb8.jpg
Let’s take a closer look at the cards.

Card Content:
[olist]
 Position: The position this player is eligible to occupy on the field. 
 Card Level: Each card can be increased in level up to level 10. We will talk more about leveling cards later in this blog. 
 Personality (only on front): Each player has two personality traits that will give them a slight increase to a specific stat if paired with other players that have the same trait. This is referred to as “chemistry” in your roster. When a card reaches level 10, it receives an additional personality trait. 
 Archetype: Each position has different archetypes that dictate what attributes the player is best at and which ones progress the fastest while leveling up. For example, linebackers can be either pass coverage, balanced, or run stoppers. 
 Primary Attributes: A player’s primary attributes are the three most important attributes to the player’s archetype.  
 Secondary Attributes (only on back): Secondary attributes are the next most important attributes for the archetype. 
 Overall: The overall rating of the player, representing his general ability. 
 Name: Player names (as well as info and appearance) can be edited in the customization menu found by pressing V when the card is selected. 
 Rarity: A card’s rarity dictates its starting overall and overall cap when increased to max level. The higher the rarity, the higher both of these numbers will be. 
[/olist]

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43609941/6d06f3ed29154bac35d712e688f13b0cb2cfd056.png
Inspecting your card will give you some additional information such as tertiary abilities (other relevant abilities that receive an upgrade at each level), full list of attributes and ratings, an explanation of the player’s archetype and personality traits, as well a list of their relevant statistics. This is also where you will be able to level up your cards. 

From the inspection menu, you are also able to customize your players. Rename them, update their equipment, change their number, and more. You can truly make your MPL team whatever you want them to be. 

Building Your Roster and Depth Chart

Once you have opened your initial packs, it is time to set up your roster. In order for players to be added to your depth chart, they must first be added to your roster. From your collection screen, you can see every card you’ve obtained from the packs you’ve opened. From here, you can organize and filter your cards by position, rarity, and whether or not they are in your roster. 

Your roster is the collection of players that will be available to you to field throughout the game and your depth chart determines who starts and backs up certain positions. 

As you are rostering players, be mindful of their personality traits. These are denoted by an icon in the upper right hand corner of the player’s cards. If you roster enough players with the same personality type, you will receive a small boost to specific ratings. 
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43609941/935f6ee65120adaddc61fa9c13fa30fe83a50fb8.jpg
These personality traits and corresponding ratings boosts include:

 Heart - Work Ethic - Increases stamina
 Trophy - Competitiveness - Increases speed
 Crown - Leadership - Increases acceleration
 Star - Professionalism - Increases agility
 Fire - Aggression - Increases strength


As you stack multiple starting players with matching personality types, you will receive higher attribute boosts. 

Upgrading Your Team

As you play MPL, you will want to consistently upgrade the players on your roster. You can do this in several ways. 

First, you can open card packs. While you can certainly purchase packs from the MPL shop to find new players, you can also unlock card packs and currency through daily log-in rewards and by completing challenges throughout the season. There are daily, weekly, and season-long challenges that you can track via the challenges menu in MPL. 

So, the more you play, the more you can unlock for free! 

You are also able to upgrade your existing cards by consuming unwanted cards in exchange for XP that is applied to an individual card. Each card can be leveled from 1 to 10, a number indicated in the top-right corner of card above the personality trait. Each level gives a ratings boost to the primary abilities of the card, a slightly smaller boost to the secondary abilities, and an even smaller boost to the tertiary abilities of the card. These are determined by the archetype of the card. The higher the rarity, the higher potential overall. 
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43609941/690ae4911fbf6d353400ed7cd8a1e4fd11897085.jpg
Compete Online

Once you have your roster and depth chart set, it’s time to take the field with your team. Match up against other MPL teams in fast-paced 4-minute quarter games. MPL’s matchmaking system will attempt to matchmake you with teams of a similar caliber. 

You can also compete offline against CPU opponents that get stronger the more you improve your team. 

Throughout the season, the game will track your wins, losses, best win streak, and other statistics. You’ll be able to track how you stack up against the field using the in-game leaderboard. The more you play and win, the higher you will climb throughout the season. 
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43609941/1a643c0a349f3b6fe7e2ee07ae946b2a9140b37b.jpg
Play Maximum Pro League on November 7th

Maximum Football releases with Exhibition, Dynasty Mode, and Maximum Pro League to Steam Early Access on November 7th. Wishlist the game now and join the Discord server to get ready for the launch next month!

notes.title: Maximum Football Comes to Steam Early Access November 7th
notes.content:
We won’t bury the lede. Maximum Football is coming to Steam Early Access on November 7th! We announced Maximum Football’s return back in 2021, and over the last three years, we have built a realistic, physics-based simulation football game from the ground up. The journey has been a long one, and we want to thank you for your patience and continued support.

November 7th marks an exciting moment for both our team and for everyone who has been eagerly waiting for Maximum Football to release. 

But this isn’t the end of anything. In fact, this is just the start of the work we’ve been promising from the beginning - building the best football simulation available WITH YOU!
[previewyoutube=nQVHqbfC3Gk;full][/previewyoutube]

What is included in Early Access?
The Early Access build will be loaded with a variety of features and modes from the jump. On November 7th, you will be have access to the following: 
[olist]
 Exhibition Mode: Play a head-to-head match up with any of the 130 pre-made teams in Maximum Football or your own created teams. 
 College Dynasty: Take over as your program’s Coach and Athletic Director in this fully customizable mode. Scout, recruit, gameplan, and manage your college’s football budget and facilities to lead your team to glory. If you missed our Dynasty Deep Dive, you can check it out here. 
 Online Multiplayer: Face off against other Maximum Football players in online head-to-head. 
 The Maximum Football Customization Suite: Create a team, create a player, and edit every aspect of your team in Maximum Football’s robust and unparalleled creation studio. All available within the game! 
[/olist]

More modes will follow shortly, such as Franchise Mode (professional football), with much more planned over the coming months and years as Maximum Football continues to evolve. Your feedback will help shape the game and balance the competitive play, so we encourage you to provide feedback and input via the official Maximum Football Discord and X to assist in creating the best football game possible.

Why Early Access on Steam only?
Early Access is an important tool for us to gather feedback directly from you, the community, so we can make the most realistic, physics-based football simulation game possible by the time we are ready for our big release on console and PC 1.0. As the community gets their hands on Maximum Football for the first time in November, there are certain to be improvements, bugs, and additional features that you will want to address, and we will use this to make the game better. 

Steam’s Early Access program gives us the ability to 1. Get Maximum Football in your hands faster and 2. take your feedback and iterate on the game more quickly over time to help us reach full release faster. By the time we reach 1.0 on other platforms, Maximum Football will have changed for the better based on early adopters’ feedback. 
Get Ready For Maximum Football
Maximum Football releases on November 7th, but you can get ready for the game today. Wishlist it on Steam, join the Maximum Football Discord server, and follow us on social media. We will have tons more to share over the next two months, so stay tuned.

notes.title: Everything You Need to Know About Dynasty in Maximum Football
notes.content:
We have said from the start that the biggest difference between Maximum Football and other football games on the market is that it will include both College Football and Professional Football. When the game launches into Early Access, you will have your first opportunity to get your hands on our College Football mode Dynasty. 

In Maximum Football’s Dynasty mode, you will serve your university in two capacities: Coach and Athletic Director. This allows you an unprecedented level of control over decisions on how to take your team to glory. Throughout the years (which there is no limit to how many seasons you can play), your league will evolve. 

In this blog, we’re highlighting how Maximum Football will give you the ability to create the college football universe you want to and take your program from the bottom of the barrel to the mountaintop of hoisting a championship trophy.

Dynasty Set-Up

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43609941/571c99c51df105a2c266131ca094c610146b6211.jpg
Pick Team
The biggest decision for your dynasty journey will be selecting which team you’d like to take over. Do you want to go for back-to-back championships with an existing powerhouse or take a low-rated team and build them up over time?

From the pick-a-team menu, you can select from the 130 premade teams, or import your own to replace one of them.. When we say that you can make the league you’ve always dreamed of, we mean it. You can replace all 130 teams with ones of your own design if you would like to.

Each team has a few traits you will want to pay attention to in this menu:

 Overall, Offense, and Defense Ratings: These are pretty simple and straightforward. These numbers represent the aggregate skill level of the players that make up the team to start. 
 Conference: The conference you participate in will determine the level of competition that you face throughout your conference schedule. More on conferences in the next section. 
 Location: Your team’s location will play an important role in recruiting players to come to your program. More on that later in the blog. 
 Total Budget: Each school has its own preset starting budget. This budget will be used for hiring your coach, and upgrading your stadium and facilities. Obviously, the higher the budget the more freedom you will have to make these upgrades early on.

Customize Conferences
Next, you can customize your conferences. Move teams around, rename conferences, and upload custom logos for each of the 12 conferences. Each conference is assigned an overall rank based on the aggregate overalls of the teams in the conference. As you move teams around, those overalls will reflect the strength of the new schools being added and removed from the conference.

Each conference also has a rank. You can edit these ranks manually from the set up menu or select an option to automatically assign ranks based on overall of the adjusted conferences.

Maximum Football’s default conference realignment system works using a relegation-promotion system. The bottom two teams in a conference at the end of the season are demoted to the conference that ranks below the one they were in while the top two from the conference will move to the conference that ranks right above the one they competed in the year prior.

Of course, you will also have the option to manually realign conferences at the end of the season, but more on that later.

Pick a Coach
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43609941/62f15b3ba207e064d0f07ea60a591474781ed9d6.jpg
Your coach will define every aspect of your teambuilding and Xs and Os strategy. On this screen, you will see quite a bit of relevant information that will shape your program’s future.

 Coach Level: The coach's level of experience. The higher the coach's level, the higher their cost to hire. However, the increased level also means they will come with better ratings and abilities. 
 Offense and Defensive Playbook: These are the offensive and defensive schemes that each coach will have your team adopt. These can be changed once you start your dynasty. 
 Overall Record: This is the coach’s career record before being hired by your school. 
 Coach Ratings: Scouting, Charisma, Stability, Player Development, Reputation, Consistency of Success
 Cost of Hiring: The one-time cost of hiring your coach. For schools with a lower starting budget, you will have to decide on a cheaper coach that may have lower ratings.


League Settings
On the final set-up screen, you are presented with several additional options for your league. These include:

 Preseason Duration: Choose the number of weeks you would like preseason to last. Each week you will be able to recruit, scout, and upgrade players. 
 Regular Season Duration: Choose how many weeks you would like the season to last. 
 League Size: Reduce the number of teams competing in your league from the default 130. 
 Playoffs Bracket Size: Determine whether you want 4, 16, or 32 teams competing at the end of the season for the championship trophy. 
 Quarter Duration: Choose how long each quarter will last. 
 Accelerated Clock: This setting causes the play clock to fast forward to a set time after play selection, allowing you to play longer quarters while maintaining a more realistic number of plays each team runs. 
 Conference Realignment: Choose how often conferences will relegate and promote teams.


Preseason
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43609941/4747f3460d875ebcca25586b7af433dc8fd89c1b.jpg
Now that your dynasty is set-up, it’s time to turn your sights toward your team. Preseason is the time to assess your players, fill your recruiting board, and take stock of your school’s facilities and stadium. All of these will have a major impact on the growth and success of your program.

Roster Set-Up
The first thing that you should do when you start your dynasty is take a look at your roster. Assess where your team’s strengths and weaknesses lie, redshirt players to keep an extra year of eligibility, set your depth chart and cut players who you don’t see having a role in your program’s future.

Recruiting
Recruiting is the lifeblood of college football. Being able to scout talent and convince them that their best chance at success is at your school is what separates competitive programs from perennial failures. In Maximum Football, our goal is for you to learn about and build relationships with your recruits throughout the season as you pitch for them to come to your school.

Setting up your Recruiting Board
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43609941/e6d1e0264981ce646088195e77b7a0fa1e356dad.jpg
The first step to building your recruiting class is identifying prospects that are interested in your school and match your school’s needs, so that you can add them to your recruiting board. At the start of preseason, all information about recruits besides their name, position, home state, and recruit rank are hidden. You will need to use “Prestige” during recruiting to unlock vital information about recruits and take actions to increase their interest in your program.

The best place to start recruiting is in your school’s home state. Recruits who live closer to your campus are more likely to be interested in attending your school. The first unlock on a recruit will reveal a bevy of useful information that will help you decide if you want to further pursue that player. This info includes their height, weight, interest level, recruit grade, and several different combine results that give key information about their rating potential.

This initial report will also let you see if the recruit has hidden upside.

Continuing to spend Prestige points here will start to reveal the actual ratings of the recruit.

Once you’ve identified talented players with interest in your school, you can add them to your recruiting board.

Building Interest
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43609941/3f5b502b367e0a3f8c15b1bb94242f2b1d421f51.jpg
Each week, you will accrue more Prestige points that can be spent on scouting recruits and building their interest in attending your school. There are multiple ways to interact with your recruits that require varying levels of Prestige investment. The goal in recruiting is to find talented players, identify what is motivating their decision, and make your school seem like the best option for them. Here are the actions you can take each week:
[olist]
 Contact: Start learning more about your recruit by contacting them. There are three methods of contact, each with their own purpose. 
 Email: When you email a recruit, you can choose up to three pitches to either unlock the prospect’s interest level in that area or influence it to become more important to the client. 
 Text Message: Text message conversations with your recruit allow you to focus on individual areas of interest and talk more specifically about the parts of your program that might sway your recruits interest. These are low-risk, low-reward ways to steadily build interest over time. 
 Call: Calling a prospect allows you to make either a soft or hard pitch for one of the areas of interest. These can be a great way to push your recruits' interest in your school forward. But if you make too hard a pitch before building that relationship, it can have a detrimental effect on your efforts. 
 Scholarship: Once your recruit’s interest level increases enough, you can offer your recruit a scholarship to come to your school. This action will also make an impact on your recruit’s interest level. 
 Visit: Finally, you can invite your recruit to visit an upcoming game at your school. The success of this visit rests on pitches that you select to give your recruit during his visit and the result of the game he attends.
[/olist]

In-Season
Now that your head coach has been hired, your roster and depth chart tweaked, and your preseason recruiting board set up, it’s time to kickoff the season. Each week you will face a new opponent and try your best to climb the national ranks and win your conference. There are plenty of off-the-field responsibilities you will have to tend to throughout the season.

Recruiting
The bulk of your recruiting responsibilities will take place throughout the season. Each week, you will be given more Prestige points to spend on scouting recruits, pitching your school, and scheduling visits. Each year, you will have 25 scholarships to hand out, so choose who you offer to carefully. 

XP
Throughout the season, you will accrue XP in a variety of manners. You will earn XP through your on-field performance week to week and for completing game, season, and career coaching challenges. XP is used to upgrade your players and your coach.

 XP can be used to directly upgrade player stats from the “Improve Players” menu. 
 Unlock new coaching skills using XP. There are two main ways to improve your coach through these skill trees.
 Upgrade Coaching: The higher your coaching level the more effective your coach becomes at influencing recruits. 
 Skill Areas: The ratings in Maximum Football roll up into 7 main categories: core, passing, rushing, receiving, blocking, defense, and special teams. Upgrading your coach in any of these areas reduces the XP cost of upgrades in that category.

Money
In the same way that your program will accrue XP week to week, your school will earn and spend money each week. You will want to make sure that you are bringing in more money than you are spending in order to have profits to spend on improving your stadium and facilities. Let’s take a look at how you will earn money and how you will spend it.

Income
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43609941/4522f8589dcc8841f7eec7f49e4d9bbfc6a67606.jpg
Your team’s income comes from 7 sources:
[olist]
 Conference Distribution: Each year, your school will receive a payment from your conference that scales depending on the prestige of your conference. 
 Government Support: Each year, every team across the league will get an on time payment from the government to upgrade their school. 
 Merchandise: During the game, your team shop will sell items like jerseys, posters, and helmets, all of which you will be able to adjust the price of. 
 Food Carts: You can choose to have as many or as few food carts as you’d like to serve your fans. Increasing the number of Food Carts at your stadium will increase the number of orders that can be placed during each game, but adding carts will also increase the upkeep cost for your stadium to run each week. 
 Ticket Sales: You control the price of your tickets and each week, you can see how many of your available seats sold. Price your tickets too high and you won’t sell enough tickets. Price them too low and you won’t be able to cover your expenses. Attendance will also fluctuate based on the performance of your team. So if you are 1-5 going into Week 7, you might want to lower the price of tickets. 
 Bowl Distribution: If your team reaches a bowl game at the end of the year, they will get a cut of the revenue generated from that event. This increases if you win the bowl. 
 Championship Distribution: If you qualify for the post-season playoff, your team will receive a cut of the revenue based on how many rounds you made it through.
[/olist]
Expenses
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43609941/b9133e2cb85afb518b5c05b314d40091eca21df4.jpg
The expenses that factor into your net income week to week include:
[olist]
 College Upkeep: This is the cost to maintain your facilities (outside of your stadium). As you upgrade your facilities, the cost of their upkeep will rise. 
 Game Expenses: These are the costs accrued by your team for each game they participate in, home or away. 
 Merch Store Upkeep: This is the cost of stocking items in your merch store. 
 Food Cart Upkeep: The cost of maintaining each food cart.
 Stadium Upkeep: As you upgrade your stadium and attract more fans, more money will be spent on maintaining your stadium. These costs only accrue during weeks with home games. 
 Coach and Staff: The cost of paying the salaries of your Coach and additional staff.
[/olist]
Money is important in your Maximum Football dynasty because it allows you to upgrade your stadium, facilities, and coaching staff. 

Stadium: There are two ways to upgrade your stadium. 

 First, you can build a new stadium that seats more fans, allowing for more ticket revenue. 
 Next, you can upgrade the tier of your stadium. Doing this will add new amenities to your stadium for fans to enjoy. Things like expanded parking, larger scoreboards, and upgraded wi-fi will make the fan experience better. This increases the amount of money your fans will spend at your stadium each week but also increases the cost of upkeep. 

Facilities: Similar to how coaches can be upgraded through XP to impact player progression, you can use money to upgrade your facilities to the same effect. Upgrade facilities for core, passing, rushing, receiving, blocking, defense, and special teams to lower the XP cost of upgrading your player’s stats in these areas. Upgrading these facilities also dynamically changes the facility grade for your program in recruiting.

Weekly Match-Up
Funny to think that we are 2,500 words into this blog and just now starting to talk about on-the-field play, but that’s just a testament to the level of depth and control you have in your Dynasty.

Each week, you will take on a different opponent to try to climb the ranks to college football glory, and even with this, you have full control over! You have several options for playing your game each week.
[olist]
 Play: You can play the game outright. Take control of your team and lead them to victory. 
 Spectate: Want to sit back and watch the fruits of your labor? Spectate the game to watch the CPU play the CPU. Note: You can also spectate any playoff, bowl or championship games - even when your own team isn’t involved.  
 Simulate: Skip the game entirely and let Maximum Football’s sim engine decide the winner.
[/olist]
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43609941/6bb4c42ee6f01f65512c6ba0e54cec8a845e0803.jpg
In this menu, you can also choose to allow the CPU to apply earned XP and handle any unspent recruiting points. In the “Coaching Info” menu, you can change the recruitment priorities for the simulation choosing to prioritize high ranking prospects, filling team needs, and going after local prospects.

Bowl Season
At the end of each season, if you’ve put together a successful regular season campaign, you will find yourself in your conference championship taking on the other top team in your conference. Qualifying for this game isn’t just about bragging rights. The top two teams in the conference will receive a chunk of revenue generated from the game with the winner receiving even more.

If your team is good enough to make it to the College Football Championship Tournament at the end of the year, you will be seeded based on your end of year ranking and take on a wave of competition to compete for the trophy. For every round you advance, your team will earn additional revenue, with a championship obviously resulting in the largest amount. This is also a great time to continue to earn XP towards player and coach progression as you compete while most other teams are watching from home.

If you missed out on a chance to compete in the tournament, your team could still qualify to compete in a bowl. These bowl games are also fully customizable! Rename the bowl and upload your own logo to replace the logos that exist in the game to create your own Bowl Season.

Off-Season
Once the postseason wraps up, you will have a few tasks to take care of prior to starting your next season.

High School All-Star Game
You’ve spent the entire year trying to convince the top high school athletes in the country to attend your school. Now, you can see them in action for the first time before they arrive on campus in the High School All-Star Game. You can either play the game outright or spectate and watch how the incoming class competes on the field.

Conference Realignment
Depending on how frequently you have set conference realignment, you will be able to view the promotion and relegation of teams around the country.

Play Drills
Each offseason, you will have the opportunity to complete a series of drills. Completing these drills will earn you additional XP that can be applied to your coach or used to upgrade your players.

More to Come
Phew. That’s a lot of details! And there is certainly more to discover when you get your hands on Dynasty later this year. We can’t wait to see the leagues, teams, players, and storylines you create when you play Maximum Football’s Dynasty Mode. This mode, as with everything else in Maximum Football, will grow and evolve through early access and beyond.

Do you have questions about Dynasty Mode or want to connect with our community to see the College football universes that they create? Join our Discord to talk with the devs, see community team creations, and offer feedback and suggestions about the game.

notes.title: 6 Ways We Are Improving Maximum Football From the Beta
notes.content:
The Maximum Football Open Beta was a HUGE success. As a top-50 played game during Next Fest, we had no shortage of players offering insightful feedback on how we can improve the game. Here’s a list of six areas we are currently working on which will improve the game in the lead up to Early Access thanks to your participation in the Beta. 

You can watch the video about these improvement below or continue reading to learn about what we will be tackling as we prepare for Early Access. 

[previewyoutube=_gdYKQt0M6E;full][/previewyoutube]
Game Pace
Game pace was an issue we addressed with the week 2, real-world speed update. While the change was largely well-received, it was a very quick change without the correct engineering behind it to commit it to the game. We’re working on that now alongside other areas of the game which need to change in order to properly support real-world speed. These include tweaking the physics, making adjustments to how acceleration works in the game, and ensuring there is a difference in feel from running and sprinting. 

Graphics, Animation and Audio
We received an abundance of positive feedback about the visuals and animations in the game, but we still have some work to do to bring this up to where we want it to be. This includes camera work, particle effects, weather, and dirt. All of these will add to the visual fidelity of the game. 

We are also still working on our full suite of animations that we have captured for the game, as well as adding even more mocaped animations which we’re sure you’ll love in our Early Access.

Player Controls
The controls in Maximum Football are also being revised in the lead up to Early Access with a few goals in mind: 
[olist]
 Create smoother controls
 Make the gameplay feel more responsive to user inputs
 Provide the user with better tutorials and practice modes to master the controls 
[/olist]
AI Players and Play calling
Limiting the Beta to gameplay against the CPU meant that we were able to gather a bevy of feedback regarding the AI play calling and execution. 

With this feedback, we’re improving the AI coaching’s situational awareness, especially as it relates to clock management at the  end of a half and in late game situations. 

Playbooks
Hand-in-hand with AI play calling, we are already on our way to improving the plays available to call as well as the actual 11-on-11 execution of the plays. We will also look into improving the in-game playart in both the play calling menu and the on-field view. 

These updates will require certain considerations before we  add custom playbooks and play creation to the game. 

UI
We want to make sure Maximum Football is user-friendly and easy to navigate. Many of you commented on the UI needing some improvements. 

We are currently doing a full audit of the accessibility of our UI and looking for ways to improve it. 

As you can see, we’ve got a football field of work ahead of us as we move towards Early Access. We can’t wait to show you how YOUR FEEDBACK has created real change in Maximum Football.
