notes.title: We're Extending the Open Beta With Build Updates!
notes.content:
Hi Maximum Football Community

The past week has been incredible! Seeing you get your hands on the game and share your thoughts about the good, the bad, and the ugly is exactly what this first public playtest was designed for. And you all showed up in a big way for us!

We have received tons of responses to our survey (if you haven't had a chance to fill that out, you can find it here), not to mention the comments that we've seen on the Steam community forums, X, Instagram, YouTube, Discord, and Reddit.

We want to make one thing absolutely clear; WE ARE LISTENING! 

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43609941/36cf7ebb53d0ab51b22dce27fc8ad508f5738d27.png

It's one thing for us to say that, but it's a whole other thing for us to show it. That's why we have just released a new patch for the Maximum Football Open Beta that addresses some of the biggest concerns that we saw from the community. 

Extending the Beta
Our original plan was to run the Beta for the week of Steam Next Fest, but since you all shared great feedback and we made some changes based on that feedback, we are extending the Beta one more week! We'd love for you to share your opinions on our changes, or maybe for the first time. 

You can now play the Beta through Monday, June 24th! 

Real Speed Open Beta
One of the biggest pieces of feedback we received over the last week is that the gameplay is too slow. College and pro-level football features some of the most impressive athletes on the planet, and we want to make sure that Maximum Football feels like you are controlling these athletes. 

The biggest change users will notice is the new real world simulation speed. We have calibrated player speed around 40-yard times between 4.2 and 5.7 seconds (depending on the speed rating of the player). This will allow the users to make quick cuts and quicker changes of direction. 

Other Changes
We have made other changes based on user feedback and you can find that complete list of bug fixes in the patch notes below. Please note that because we turned around a patch in a week, we were not able to address all your feedback and bug issues. What's going on everyone! Welcome back to another Maximum Football development diary!

It feels like 100 years since our last video, but we've been grinding to make Maximum Football a true American Football Simulation video game.

With so much worked on since our last update, let's get into the massive update about AI, animations, physics, dynasty, customization, multiplayer, sfx, vfx, and so much more.

Gameplay - The Core Focus
From day one, our top priority has been authentic gameplay. It's all about creating a realistic football experience at every position. Getting basic football mechanics correct has been our goal.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43609941/e84dcd1814f89e8719b23b6d6c9367c0974ce338.png

Blocking
There have been extensive improvements in the blocking game, including the addition of pull blocks, downfield blocks, and open field blocks. Blockers can double team a defender when needed, and then detach from the double team to target a new defender when the new threat is detected. Other blocking updates include:

 Smart, dynamic blockers; size and attributes matter.
 No 3 or 4 person scenes that lock players into animations (like other football video games).
 Real-time adjustments, avoiding pre-made animation scenarios.


{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43609941/88acb4746a26ab4331737571d6c4c1d05c7570a3.png

Passing
We've added realistic QB styles, from pocket passing to throw-on-the-run style QBs.
Maximum Footballs' Advanced AI helps to identify open receivers and allow QBs with certain attributes to throw with more accuracy/power.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43609941/e279a00311a8b8a07eacda2aad282a4719f5db8e.png

Catching
We've enhanced receiver attributes to help determine everything from how the receiver handles being pressed to how well the receiver can catch the football. Receivers can now adjust routes on the fly when passes are inaccurate or contested. We've also added hundreds of catching animations.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43609941/63dab466e3b7b92466efb1a252ee26e59f6e9dd9.png

Running Game
For the running game, we've added the following mechanics.

 Smooth, responsive ball carrier mechanics.
 AI-led gap identification even in chaotic situations.
 Differentiated moves for power backs (stiff arm/truck) versus Speed backs (spin/juke)


Defense
On the defensive side of the ball, we've made the following improvements. 

 Improved man and zone coverage AI.
 Defensive gap assignment AI
 Advanced presnap adjustments, audibles, and player positioning.
 Attributes-driven play prediction and reaction.
 Physics tackles

Question: What is Early Access?
Answer: Early Access is a place where games are playable in an alpha or beta state while they are under continued development. Games in Early Access should be considered unfinished. The reason for Early Access is it allows gamers to play and provide feedback to help shape a game and its features.

Question: When is Early Access available?

Answer: We believe that providing access to players in an early state allows us to gather crucial feedback from the community to build the best possible experience.

notes.title: EARLY ACCESS
notes.content:
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43609941/7bf22f72fe32e0dff464bd39e3b2dc2cf1d076ed.jpg

Maximum Football Community,

We can't express enough gratitude for the excitement and anticipation shown from you all for Maximum Football. Our ambition for this project from the start has been to create a Free to Play, Physics Driven, Customizable football experience within deep Collegiate and Pro atmospheres. To that end, the development team is working hard to deliver a new and exciting experience at the quality level that meets this ambition and lets you etch your own story in sports greatness.
Therefore, after much evaluation, the team has decided to move the Steam Early Access launch to Fall of 2023.

We share your passion for gaming and the sport of football, and we know this is the right decision for Maximum Football and its fans. Thank you for your patience in waiting a little bit longer to get on the field.

Look for more in-depth information as we get closer to Early Access, and follow our social media channels and join our Discord for more updates.

The Maximum Football Team 

PS: Check out our GAMEPLAY progress! First look! 

[previewyoutube=u6dIneeeVP0;full][/previewyoutube]

Question: Why the delay? 
Answer: Even though we’ve been pleased with the progress of development thus far, we feel that to deliver a title that meets or exceeds expectations more time is needed for development.

Question: What is Early Access? 
Answer: Early Access is a place where games are playable in an alpha or beta state while they are under continued development. Games in Early Access should be considered unfinished. The reason for Early Access is it allows gamers to play and provide feedback to help shape a game and its features.

Question: When is Early Access available? 
Answer: Fall of 2023

Question: Why bring MXFB to Steam Early Access instead of releasing the full game? 
Answer: We believe that providing access to players in an early state allows us to gather crucial feedback from the community to build the best possible experience.

Question: Is GAMEPLAY still your focus? 
Answer: Yes! Gameplay has always been our focus for Maximum Football. We have been polishing and tweaking our gameplay as seen with recent DEV DIARIES and NOTES. We are incredibly passionate about getting it right and nailing a formula you’ll enjoy. It’s one of the prime reasons for the delay. We want to turn a few more screws before unleashing it in Early Access.

notes.title: DEVELOPER NOTE Ep. 3
notes.content:
Bring it in team! Bring it in! 

In another DEV NOTE, we hear from Micah our Development Director. He talks about the Quarterback and how defenders will treat him based off of his "THREAT" level!  


{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43609941/445f749ef89f1c88d85ad01c53f38fba329f0a53.jpg

🚧 Work in Progress 🚧

“The QB is either a low, medium or high running threat depending on how close he is to the line of scrimmage, how close he is to the hash’s, and how fast he is moving. The faster he is and the closer he is to the LOS the more threat.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43609941/7720ee6515629c2b5bba4ef8f79b2b86125afbb8.jpg

Defenders will behave differently depending on the threat level of the QB. If he is a high threat they will abandon their responsibilities and chase him. If its a medium threat they will pursue the quarterback if they have no one else to guard.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43609941/3ee74fd997a0079d47a41b72a253553dbe043243.jpg

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43609941/f7cfbea60640203a627ce063c2e441a10de00ec6.jpg

If the QB is a low threat the defenders will simply shade towards him without abandoning their current responsibilities. The red, yellow and orange circles indicate which defenders will react to the QB threat levels.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43609941/f0554bbf6058575ef24ac0f733af2373b64f256c.jpg

If the QB is a High threat and the defender is within the Red circle then he will pursue the QB using the High Threat level AI. If the defender is in the Orange circle when the QB is a Medium Threat then the defender will behave with Medium Threat Level AI. If the defender is in the Yellow circle when the QB is a Low Threat then the defender will behave with Low Threat Level AI.”

Micah Brown
Development Director
